column3: Close to the Hebrew; “a strange woman” is rendered “an immoral woman.”
Close to the Hebrew; “a sword of mouths” is rendered “a two-edged sword.”
Close to the Hebrew; שְׁאוֹל (“Sheol”) is rendered “hell.”
The verse is difficult; NKJV takes the subject as “you,” “Lest you ponder her path of life,” and “they wander” as “are unstable.”
Close to the Hebrew; הוֹדֶךָ (“your vigor, splendor”) is rendered “your honor.”
Close to the Hebrew; “I was almost in every evil” is rendered “I was on the verge of total ruin.”
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV renders the line as a question, “Should your fountains be dispersed abroad.”
Close to the Hebrew; “a doe of loves and a mountain goat of grace” is rendered “a loving deer and a graceful doe,” and “be intoxicated” “be enraptured.”
Close to the Hebrew; “strange woman” and “foreign woman” are rendered “an immoral woman” and “a seductress,” and “go astray” “be enraptured.”
Close to the Hebrew; מְפַלֵּס (“makes level, weighs”) is rendered “He ponders.”
